name: University of Connecticut
header:
University of Connecticut
United States · Mathematics PhD
Rank verification is maintained separately.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• New English waiver needs graded credit/GPA criteria, not F-1 status.
• TA English oral qualification remains even if admission test waived.
• Jeremy Teitelbaum remains a professor with substantial historical work on p-adic groups, elliptic curves and
modular forms, but his official page now emphasizes bioinformatics and machine learning. Confirm current
arithmetic PhD interests before treating the historical specialization as an active opening. Recent topical paper
metadata was not established here [faculty_teitelbaum].
• Faculty below form a verified research-fit shortlist, not a complete census. New-student supervision and 2027
leave/moves must be confirmed; paper dates describe the cited version.
• No 2022-2026 original article verified. The 2025 award does not turn the 2016 Wu-Yau paper into a 2025
publication; retain 2020 complex-geometry anchor as well.
• No original paper newer than the 2022 article verified. The old personal bibliography is incomplete, not
evidence that publication stopped in 2014.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Strong undergraduate math program; accredited bachelor’s and GPA ≥3.0 degree-wide, or 3.0 last two years,
or 3.5 last year (exceptions possible). International students welcomed. [s1] [s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Use Graduate School portal; prepare 1-2 page personal statement and three academic letters. Math opts out of
foreign third-party credential evaluations; no need to order one for UChicago. [s1]
Adviser contact [Unresolved]
No public requirement to secure an adviser before submitting was established in the admissions pages
checked. Use the research-fit shortlist for potential contacts and confirm 2027 availability/graduate supervision
eligibility. A faculty listing does not promise an opening. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Portal workflow [Unresolved]
Graduate School application/status portal; submitted before letter receipt allowed. Referees must submit
electronically; exact invitation trigger/update/reuse unpublished. [s2] [s3]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Program December 15 year unspecified; English waiver explicit Spring 2027+ and pay chart 2027-28. [s1] [s2]
[s6]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
Old TOEFL 79/new 4.5; IELTS 6.5, PTE 60, DET 110; 2 year validity at application. Official agency reports; no
TOEFL MyBest/Essentials or IELTS One Skill Retake. TA oral English proof separate even if admission waived.
[s2]
UChicago English exemption [2027 confirmed]
Effective Spring 2027+:≥30 graded U.S. undergraduate (or combined) credits by matriculation and cumulative
GPA ≥3.0 in all U.S. work qualifies. P/F, audit, credit, incomplete excluded. UChicago study should qualify if
thresholds met; documentation required. [s2]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not required; voluntary-score handling unpublished. [s1]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Not required explicitly including mathematics subject. Voluntary-score handling unpublished. [s1]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [2027 confirmed]
2027-28 official 100% GA (20 h/week) Level 1:$31, 228.28 for Aug 23, 2027-May 21, 2028(19.5 pay periods),
$1601.45 biweekly. Level 2$32, 860.04; Level 3$36, 534.03. Tuition waived, health subsidized; student fees
payable. These are standard appointment rates, not guaranteed offer/summer funds. [s6] [s7]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Normally up to 5 years, conditional on funds, department needs/policies, progress, job performance and
eligibility; extension case by case. [s5]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International applicants encouraged and GA path available; TA oral English qualification required regardless of
admission waiver. Specific fellowship citizenship conditions must be checked. [s1] [s2] [s7]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Regular status, full-time, GPA ≥3.0, registration eligible; first fall TA training Math 5000. Standard GA 10-20
hours/week, usually 9 months. [s5] [s7]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
TA usually offered with PhD admission; RA depends faculty funds. Separate fellowship extras not established.
[s5]
Other funding routes [Unresolved]
Math advertises GAANN for financial need/academic merit; exact eligibility requires award check and must not
be assumed available to F-1. [s5]

Application fee [Standing rule]
$75 nonrefundable credit card; application not complete until paid or waived. [s2]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Central qualifying affiliations/military categories; programs may pay limited fees for exceptional candidates -
ask math. Wait 3-5 business days after application before querying waiver; no refunds if paid first. [s4]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Aurel-Mihai (Mihai) Fulger
Positivity of divisors, cycles and vector bundles; base loci, Seshadri constants, and Newton-Okounkov bodies.
[faculty1] [faculty1a]
Associate Professor; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2025 · Positivity and base loci of vector bundles revisited
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Álvaro Lozano-Robledo
Elliptic curves and abelian varieties, Mordell-Weil groups and Galois representations, especially complex
multiplication and division fields. [faculty3] [faculty3a]
Professor; new website linked from official UConn page, availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint · The image of the adelic Galois representation of an elliptic curve with complex
multiplication
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Complex geometry / geometric analysis
Damin Wu
Kähler-Einstein geometry, holomorphic curvature and positivity of canonical bundles, geometric PDE; also
spaces of Riemannian metrics. [faculty5] [faculty5a] [gapc50] [gapc51] [gapc52]
UConn faculty with university-hosted research and publications pages; retain rank from base dossier.
Research evidence: 2020; official list last updated January 2022 · Invariant metrics on negatively pinched complete Kähler
manifolds
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Research evidence: 2021 journal; 2019 preprint · Contractibility results for certain spaces of Riemannian metrics on the disc
Alessandro Carlotto and Damin Wu, Mathematical Research Letters 28 (2021), 1033-1045; current official author bibliography
verifies publication year. This is Riemannian geometric analysis rather than specifically complex geometry.
Evidence history and corrections (earlier statements may be superseded)
 Earlier group: Complex geometry

Earlier interests: Kähler geometry, curvature and canonical bundles, invariant metrics, and nonlinear geometric PDE. The
most recent directly verified topical paper on his official list is from 2020; a newer research-paper census remains
unverified.
Earlier appointment: Professor; recent 2025 departmental award news confirms affiliation but does not establish a new
paper. Availability unconfirmed.
Evidence qualifications
No 2022-2026 original article verified. The 2025 award does not turn the 2016 Wu-Yau paper into a 2025 publication; retain 2020
complex-geometry anchor as well.
Representation theory
Kyu-Hwan Lee
Quantum and Kac-Moody algebras, cluster algebras, arithmetic statistics and AI-assisted number theory;
recent publications connect quantum cluster structures with Grothendieck rings. [faculty7] [faculty7a]
Professor at UConn and KIAS Scholar; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Quantum cluster algebra, braid moves and quantum virtual Grothendieck ring
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Ralf Schiffler
Quiver representations, cluster algebras, categorification, quantum affine algebras and geometric models for
syzygies. [faculty9] [faculty9a]
Professor; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Real simple modules over simply-laced quantum affine algebras and categorifications of cluster
algebras
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Number theory / algebra
Keith Conrad
Number theory and arithmetic over number and function fields; verified newer work also concerns Lie-algebra
actions and harmonic polynomials over commutative rings. [faculty11] [faculty11a] [faculty_conrad_publisher] [gapc53]
[gapc54] [gapc55] [gapc56]
Associate Professor in UConn's official faculty profile.
Research evidence: 2022 · Rotational symmetries in polynomial rings
Primary publisher record corroborates a newer paper absent from the official faculty list; not a recent number-theory paper.
Evidence history and corrections (earlier statements may be superseded)
 Earlier group: Number theory
Earlier interests: Number theory, including arithmetic of polynomial values and function fields. Official publications page is
stale (latest listed 2014); no recent paper from that page was established. A 2022 algebra paper is separately available
from its publisher.
Earlier appointment: Associate Professor; current research direction and PhD openings require direct confirmation.
Evidence qualifications
No original paper newer than the 2022 article verified. The old personal bibliography is incomplete, not evidence that publication
stopped in 2014.

text:
University of Connecticut
United States · Mathematics PhD
Rank verification is maintained separately.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• New English waiver needs graded credit/GPA criteria, not F-1 status.
• TA English oral qualification remains even if admission test waived.
• Jeremy Teitelbaum remains a professor with substantial historical work on p-adic groups, elliptic curves and
modular forms, but his official page now emphasizes bioinformatics and machine learning. Confirm current
arithmetic PhD interests before treating the historical specialization as an active opening. Recent topical paper
metadata was not established here [faculty_teitelbaum].
• Faculty below form a verified research-fit shortlist, not a complete census. New-student supervision and 2027
leave/moves must be confirmed; paper dates describe the cited version.
• No 2022-2026 original article verified. The 2025 award does not turn the 2016 Wu-Yau paper into a 2025
publication; retain 2020 complex-geometry anchor as well.
• No original paper newer than the 2022 article verified. The old personal bibliography is incomplete, not
evidence that publication stopped in 2014.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Strong undergraduate math program; accredited bachelor’s and GPA ≥3.0 degree-wide, or 3.0 last two years,
or 3.5 last year (exceptions possible). International students welcomed. [s1] [s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Use Graduate School portal; prepare 1-2 page personal statement and three academic letters. Math opts out of
foreign third-party credential evaluations; no need to order one for UChicago. [s1]
Adviser contact [Unresolved]
No public requirement to secure an adviser before submitting was established in the admissions pages
checked. Use the research-fit shortlist for potential contacts and confirm 2027 availability/graduate supervision
eligibility. A faculty listing does not promise an opening. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Portal workflow [Unresolved]
Graduate School application/status portal; submitted before letter receipt allowed. Referees must submit
electronically; exact invitation trigger/update/reuse unpublished. [s2] [s3]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Program December 15 year unspecified; English waiver explicit Spring 2027+ and pay chart 2027-28. [s1] [s2]
[s6]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [Standing rule]
PhD December 15, fall only; year/timezone not explicit. Do not use MS January 5 deadline. [s1]

Funding consideration [Unresolved]
TAs usually offered with PhD admission; December 15 program date safest target. Separate fellowship
deadlines unverified. [s1] [s5]
Reference receipt [Unresolved]
Three letters required; submission before letters allowed, but separate letter deadline/grace unpublished.
Target December 15 and confirm. [s1] [s3]
Test-score receipt [Unresolved]
Required official tests must come directly from agency; no separate December 15 grace published. English
waiver likely relevant. [s2]
Supporting documents [Unresolved]
Program December 15; final official degree-document date and separate late document policy unverified. I-20
request at least one month before semester after admission. [s1] [s2]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
No binding program-wide acceptance deadline for Fall 2027 was established in the public admissions pages
checked. Use the individual offer and ask the program if unclear; do not infer April 15 merely from an earlier
CGS signatory list. [s1] [s2] [s3]
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
Old TOEFL 79/new 4.5; IELTS 6.5, PTE 60, DET 110; 2 year validity at application. Official agency reports; no
TOEFL MyBest/Essentials or IELTS One Skill Retake. TA oral English proof separate even if admission waived.
[s2]
UChicago English exemption [2027 confirmed]
Effective Spring 2027+:≥30 graded U.S. undergraduate (or combined) credits by matriculation and cumulative
GPA ≥3.0 in all U.S. work qualifies. P/F, audit, credit, incomplete excluded. UChicago study should qualify if
thresholds met; documentation required. [s2]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not required; voluntary-score handling unpublished. [s1]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Not required explicitly including mathematics subject. Voluntary-score handling unpublished. [s1]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload bachelor’s institution and post-bachelor’s records; international section also asks all postsecondary
coursework even without degree. Foreign records original plus English; math waives third-party evaluation
requirement. [s1] [s2]
Mathematics-course list [Unresolved]
The public admissions checklist checked does not establish a separate mathematics course-list requirement.
Confirm any portal-only supplement and its format; omission here does not mean unsolicited uploads are
permitted. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
The public admissions checklist checked does not establish a separate course-description/textbook-list
requirement. Confirm any portal-only supplement and its format; omission here does not mean unsolicited
uploads are permitted. [s1] [s2] [s3]

Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three; academic letters strongly preferred. [s1]
Scholarship references; What sends the invitation; Receipt confirmation; Updating and reusing
letters [Unresolved]
This specific reference detail was not established by the public program/graduate application instructions
checked. Confirm it in the current referee-help screen or with admissions before entering contacts; no
invitation was triggered during research. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Yes, application may be submitted before letters received. [s3]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume; Research-interest statement; Research proposal; Writing sample / thesis /
research summary; Publications list; Course-list document; Scholarship essays; Other short
answers / materials [Unresolved]
The public mathematics and graduate-admissions pages checked do not establish a separate requirement or
permission to submit this item. Required/optional status, exact prompt, length, formatting and
upload-versus-link instructions remain unverified; check the current portal before drafting or sending an extra
document. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Math calls it personal statement, 1-2 pages; paraphrase: what attracts you to program and why it fits. Upload
in application; exact font/margins not published. [s1]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Same 1-2 page program-fit personal statement; separate background essay not listed. [s1]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [2027 confirmed]
2027-28 official 100% GA (20 h/week) Level 1:$31, 228.28 for Aug 23, 2027-May 21, 2028(19.5 pay periods),
$1601.45 biweekly. Level 2$32, 860.04; Level 3$36, 534.03. Tuition waived, health subsidized; student fees
payable. These are standard appointment rates, not guaranteed offer/summer funds. [s6] [s7]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Normally up to 5 years, conditional on funds, department needs/policies, progress, job performance and
eligibility; extension case by case. [s5]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International applicants encouraged and GA path available; TA oral English qualification required regardless of
admission waiver. Specific fellowship citizenship conditions must be checked. [s1] [s2] [s7]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Regular status, full-time, GPA ≥3.0, registration eligible; first fall TA training Math 5000. Standard GA 10-20
hours/week, usually 9 months. [s5] [s7]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
TA usually offered with PhD admission; RA depends faculty funds. Separate fellowship extras not established.
[s5]
Other funding routes [Unresolved]
Math advertises GAANN for financial need/academic merit; exact eligibility requires award check and must not
be assumed available to F-1. [s5]

Application fee [Standing rule]
$75 nonrefundable credit card; application not complete until paid or waived. [s2]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Central qualifying affiliations/military categories; programs may pay limited fees for exceptional candidates -
ask math. Wait 3-5 business days after application before querying waiver; no refunds if paid first. [s4]
Conflicts and remaining checks
Conflicting sources [Standing rule]
Math specifically opts out of central foreign credential-evaluation requirement; do not order based only on
central default. [s1] [s2]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Confirm December 2026 deadline/timezone and letter cutoff; exact reference invitation/receipt/update/reuse;
portal CV/course/sample fields; offer duration and summer funding, scholarship eligibility, commitment date.
